About the role

Would you like to be part of an ambitious Compliance team where you play a key role in ensuring that Saxo meets its regulatory obligations within financial and non-financial risk areas? If so, this may be the right opportunity for you at Saxo. You will join the Prudential Oversight team within Group Compliance, Saxo's second line of defence function, based at our headquarters in Hellerup. Our team oversees compliance risks across a broad range of areas, including the financial risk areas of capital, market risk, liquidity and credit risk, as well as non-financial risk areas such as ICT, operational risk, model risk, data governance and strategy, supporting the business in meeting regulatory requirements, market standards and internal policies. Your primary responsibility will be to conduct compliance oversight and monitoring across the financial risk areas of capital, market risk, liquidity and credit risk in relation to policies, procedures, segregation of duties, limits, calculations, samples, controls, etc. As a team, we balance professionalism with a sense of humour and maintain an informal atmosphere where people enjoy coming to work.

Responsibilities

• Perform compliance risk assessments

• Provide advice and compliance opinions to the business on managing compliance risks and regulatory requirements

• Conduct compliance monitoring activities

• Contribute to regular compliance reporting to senior management of the bank

• Participate in developing the bank’s compliance framework

• Interact with the business across organisational levels and seniority

Your profile

We are looking for a colleague with experience from working with one or more prudential risk areas, who is motivated to develop deeper expertise in these areas. Further we expect you to have:

• At least 2 years of relevant experience from the financial sector, preferably within compliance, risk management, audit, finance, credit or another relevant first-line function

• A relevant educational background within economics, finance, accounting, audit or similar

• Interest in prudential risk areas such as capital, liquidity, market risk, credit risk, model risk, strategic risk, operational risk areas, governance, and internal controls

• Familiarity with regulatory requirements such as CRR/CRD, Basel guidelines, EBA/ESMA guidelines, the Executive Order on Management and Control of Banks and other relevant Danish financial regulation is an advantage

Moreover, we are looking for someone who is detail-oriented, can work independently while taking an active role in teamwork and enjoys collaborating with colleagues and stakeholders across the entire organisation. It is an advantage if you thrive in an environment with constant change, bring a positive and curious mindset to work, and do not buy into the word ‘cannot’. You must possess strong stakeholder management skills and use your communication skills to ensure positive collaboration and progress in joint tasks. We are looking for a colleague who always brings a positive attitude when liaising with the business.

Please note! International applicants are encouraged to apply. To help us understand your circumstances, we kindly ask candidates currently based outside Denmark to include a brief summary of their relocation plans and expected timeframe for relocating to Denmark.

We get curious people invested in the world

When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on. You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success. We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations. When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense. At Saxo we don’t just offer a job – we offer an opportunity to invest in your future!

How to apply

: Click here to create an account and upload your resume and a short motivation. We look forward to getting to know you better!

About Saxo Bank

Support our purpose

We believe access to global capital markets is not only for the privileged few. Our vision is to enable people to fulfill their financial aspirations to make an impact. That’s why we use the power of technology to deliver clients what they need, when they need it in a user-friendly and personalised experience. We aim to deliver the world’s most user-friendly and personalized trading and investment platform experience, which gives our clients exactly what they need to make more informed investment decisions.

Be part of a unique journey

Do you want to work for an extremely ambitious organisation at the cutting edge of banking and technology? You’ll be joining a company that:

. Continuously strives to improve the Saxo Experience and exceed our clients’ expectations.

. Always invests in the future

. Builds unrivalled platforms for seasoned and experienced investors and wholesale clients that provide real-time access to global capital markets.

. Consistently wins the highest accolades for our platforms, products and services.

Own your future

So, if you’re up for the challenge of breaking down barriers in global financial markets, we’re always looking for ambitious and enthusiastic people who share our passion for clients, technology and innovation and can bring new perspectives to our diverse team. For more on our story, culture and identity, please read the Saxo Bank Foundation, written by our CEO and founder Kim Fournais.

jobs.description:
Vattenfall is a leading European energy company driving the transition to a sustainable energy system. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years. We employ around 21 000 people mostly in our core markets in Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK.

Do you want to make a difference and help industrial companies navigate the energy transition?

Vattenfall’s Business Sales Department offers a wide range of products in the energy field. We operate in a highly competitive and dynamic market, serving large corporate customers, partners, and resellers. Our ambition is to be number one for the customer.

We are looking for a Key Account Manager to join our Industrial Production Clients team within Business Area Customers & Solutions. This is an opportunity to strengthen Vattenfall’s position as the preferred energy partner for industrial customers in Denmark and across the Nordic region.

Our customers operate in an increasingly complex environment where competitiveness, energy supply, commercial risk, and sustainability ambitions are closely connected. In this role, you will help customers navigate these challenges while building long-term partnerships that create value for both the customer and Vattenfall.

Vattenfall has established a strong position within the Industrial Production client segment in Sweden, Finland, and Denmark. As we continue to build an even stronger customer platform in Denmark, you will become an important part of our Nordic sales organization and contribute directly to its future growth.

You will join a Nordic sales team of thirteen Key Account Managers across Sweden, Finland, and Denmark and report to the Sales Manager and Head of Industrial Production Clients Nordic. Based in Copenhagen, you will work closely with colleagues across the region. The team has a collaborative, knowledge-sharing culture, supported by flexible working conditions that combine office collaboration with remote work when appropriate.

Your role

As Key Account Manager, you will be responsible for developing long-term, profitable business and strategic customer partnerships within the Nordic Industrial Production client segment. You will work with prospects and customers to understand their operations, energy needs, market exposure, decision-making structures, and long-term priorities.

From this insight, you will identify opportunities, offer relevant solutions, and negotiate contracts. You will act as a trusted advisor, helping prospects and customers navigate the energy transition, manage market risks, and achieve their sustainability ambitions, including reducing their environmental footprint.

You will coordinate cross-functional expertise across Vattenfall to develop and deliver customer solutions. This includes close cross-functional collaboration to ensure alignment, a seamless customer experience, and long-term value creation.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Develop and manage long-term strategic relationships with industrial prospects & customers in Denmark and across the Nordic market.

• Identify customer needs and translate them into tailored, value-creating energy solutions.

• Take commercial ownership of customer opportunities from early development through internal alignment, negotiation, and contracting.

• Lead commercial discussions and contract negotiations in close collaboration with relevant specialists.

• Coordinate cross-functional bid and solution-development activities, ensuring clear ownership, alignment, and progress.

• Act as a trusted advisor by translating energy-market and industry developments into relevant customer insights.

Manage and develop a profitable customer portfolio while contributing to Vattenfall’s customer offering and commercial platform in Denmark.

Your profile

You are a commercially minded professional with experience in B2B sales, key account management, business development, or another field involving complex customer solutions. Experience from the energy commodity business is highly relevant, while experience from sectors with complex instruments, such as insurance or finance, may also provide a strong foundation.

You combine strategic and commercial focus with operational capability. You are genuinely interested in customers and their industry challenges, and you are motivated to create the best possible value through collaboration. Structured, proactive, and self-driven, you enjoy working independently as well as in a cross-border team.

Your credibility is built through business insight, sound judgement, and clear communication. You are trustworthy, solution-oriented, and comfortable involving the right colleagues to move customer opportunities forward. You bring creative thinking and a drive to continuously develop and improve.

To succeed in this role, you bring:

• A relevant degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Engineering, Science, or a comparable field.

• Fluency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

• Strong and demonstrated business acumen.

• Experience in B2B sales, key account management, business development, or other complex commercial environments.

• Knowledge of energy commodities, electricity markets, energy procurement, risk management, or comparable complex solutions.

• Strong communication, influencing, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.

• A genuine interest in customers, their operations, and their industry challenges.

• A proactive, collaborative, and solution-oriented way of working.

• Experience with electricity supply agreements, commodity contracts, hedging solutions, power purchase agreements, Nordic electricity markets, or decarbonisation strategies is an advantage.

• An established network within Danish industry or the energy sector would also be beneficial.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Location  Copenhagen

Our offer

Looking for a career with growth?

Looking for a role where your superpowers can be leveraged to the maximum and with limitless opportunities for growth?

The scale and ambition of our wind, battery and solar business means you can really find your element with us. We’ll also provide you with all the learning and development you need to expand your horizons.

We strive to be the best place to work in the industry with highly competitive pay and conditions and an open, supportive culture. A commitment to a healthy work-life balance aims to ensure everyone plays to their strengths, whatever their background and experiences.

You will be part of a growing team of 1,700+ colleagues from 50+ nationalities where our positive approach to diversity is reflected in the fact that more than a quarter of staff are women.

More Information

For more information about the position you are welcome to contact hiring manager Annelie Gerborn, annelie.gerborn@vattenfall.com.  For more information about the recruitment process you are welcome to contact our recruiter Christian Pathuel, christian.pathuel@vattenfall.com

We welcome your application in English no later than 22-11-2026. We kindly request that you do not send applications by any means other than via our website.

At Vattenfall we are convinced that diversity contributes to building a more profitable and attractive company and we strive to be a good role model regarding diversity. Vattenfall works actively for all employees to have the same opportunities and rights regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, transgender identity or expression, religion or other belief, disability or sexual orientation. Click here for further information.

The security of Vattenfall and its employees is essential. For that reason, a pre-employment screening will be part of your recruitment process. The screening is based on the role you will fulfill within Vattenfall and will be performed by a third party, DISA Global Solutions AB.

Since Vattenfall is a part of the Swedish critical infrastructure, many of our services are security classed. If this position is security classified the final candidates might be subject to a security vetting process, according to Swedish legislation.

We look forward to receiving your application!

_Do you enjoy turning strategic ambitions into concrete results? Would you like to help shape the future of some of the Nordics' leading private brands? Then you might be the Strategy Consultant we are looking for.

_As a Strategy Consultant, you will play a key role in moving our From Good to Great strategy forward. Working at the intersection of strategy, transformation and commercial development, you will help shape and deliver initiatives that create real impact across the business.

You will be part of our newly created Strategy and Business Development team, reporting to the General Manager working closely with colleagues across the organisation, including Procurement, Supply Chain, Design Development, Quality and PMO, while also collaborating directly with our CEO, Senior Leadership Team and Nordic Partners.

**Key Responsibilities

**The role covers a broad range of responsibilities, including:

• Manage key value streams within larger transformation programmes with responsibility for the plan, deliverables and realised benefits

• Run smaller strategic projects end-to-end, from scoping through implementation and handover to the organisation

• Structure ambiguous strategic questions into hypotheses, analyses and decision-ready recommendations for the CEO and Senior Leadership Team

• Build business cases and financial models to support prioritisation, investment decisions and benefit tracking

• Analyse category, supplier and price/value performance to support private brand and sourcing decisions

• Identify and assess new business opportunities and strategic partnerships

**To Thrive In This Role, We Imagine That You

**

• Have a relevant master’s degree, for example in business, economics, finance, strategy or a related field

• Have 2-4 years of experience in consulting or an in-house strategy, transformation or commercial function

• Are a skilled problem solver, qualitatively and quantitatively, including financial modelling and business cases

• Have a solid business understanding of how strategy affects financial, operational and commercial performance

• Have led a workstream or smaller project, managing your own plan, stakeholders and deliverables

• Are highly proficient in PowerPoint and Excel and can produce executive-level material without heavy review

• Have professional proficiency in English

• Ideally have experience in retail, FMCG, sourcing, or private brands. Proficiency in a Nordic language is also a plus.

**Personal Competencies

**You can take initiative and navigate circumstances where the path forward is not fully defined.

**In Addition, You

**

• Are organised, strategic and commercially curious

• Carry tasks through from beginning to end

• Drive tasks forward from start to finish

• Move easily between the bigger picture and operational details

• Are pragmatic and focused on turning analysis into action and results

• Build good relationships and communicate confidently with stakeholders at all levels

**What We Offer

**

• A company where people know one another well in the office and the culture is informal

• At the same time, you will be part of a larger Nordic setup, working with our four partners in Norway, Sweden, Denmark and Finland. So, while you will get to know your colleagues at our Vesterbro office well, you will build a broad network and collaborate with many different stakeholders across the Nordics

• Develop both personally and professionally, learning from skilled colleagues and partners along the way

• Be part of a purpose-driven company shaping the future of Nordic private brands for millions of consumers

If you are ready to take the next step in your career and join Coop Trading, please send us your CV no later than 13th of November 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis.

Place of work: Vesterbro, Copenhagen

We believe that a strong culture is built through spending time together. Our Vesterbro office is therefore our primary place of work, while we offer the flexibility to work from home when needed.

The role involves a limited number of travel days each year, some of which may require overnight stays.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact General Manager, S&BD, Gustav Gaarde at +45 2777 2575.

**About Us

**Coop Trading’s purpose is to make a better every day through leading Nordic private brands for 27 million Nordic consumers delivering the best quality products at a fair price. Our portfolio encompasses both food and daily non-food items within our private brands: Xtra, Coop, and Änglamark.

Coop Trading represents Coop in Sweden, Denmark, Norway, as well as SOK in Finland. Through our private brands, we are proud to be present on every third dinner table in Nordic homes. On behalf of our four partners, we develop products for our private brand portfolio through innovation, product development, and negotiating Nordic agreements.

Coop Trading is a dynamic, responsible, and ambitious workplace. We are 140 dedicated professionals in Denmark and in Spain, as well as a network of trusted partners across the Nordic region. We work to challenge the status quo delivering the best and most innovative private brand products.

A cornerstone of our identity is our continuous commitment to fostering an engaging and appreciative work environment and to being an exceptional place to work.

• Set GetWhy’s global events strategy with the marketing leadership, from tentpole industry conferences (IIEX, ESOMAR, Quirk’s) to hosted events, executive roundtables and product showcases.

• Plan, produce and execute 15–20+ events per year across Europe, the US and beyond, each tied to clear pipeline, brand and customer goals.

• Own the global events budget, sponsorship negotiations, and relationships with agencies, venues and production partners.

Make GetWhy unmissable at every conference

• Have a strong point of view on world-class conference presence, from booth concept and spatial design to merch and the small details people remember.

• Replace badge-scanning booths with live experiences: let attendees run a real GetWhy study, see AI-moderated interviews in action, and leave with an insight.

• Secure speaking slots and sponsorships that put GetWhy at the centre of the industry conversation.

Put customers on stage

• Build a flagship GetWhy-hosted event where customers present the work they’ve done with GetWhy and show other brands how to do the same.

• Recruit and prepare customer and executive speakers, and make sure every GetWhy representative on stage or on the floor is briefed and on message.

Own the side events and intimate moments

• Design VIP dinners, executive roundtables and side events around major conferences, where the real relationships are built.

• Partner with Sales and Customer Success on account-based events that move specific deals and expansions forward.

Run the content machine

• Capture on-site content at every event, including video, photos and short clips that show GetWhy’s presence on the ground.

• Turn events into social media content, such as live posts, recaps, reels and LinkedIn stories, working with the wider marketing team.

• Conduct on-site interviews with customers, speakers and industry leaders, creating content for social, the website and sales enablement.

• Make sure every event keeps working for weeks afterwards through recaps, clips and follow-up campaigns.

Turn events into revenue

• Build the pre- and post-event engine: invitations, promotion, lead capture, qualification and a seamless handoff to Sales.

• Track and report on pipeline, ROI, reach and brand impact for every event, and double down on what works.

Build the playbook

• Create scalable playbooks and “event in a box” toolkits so local teams and partners can host on-brand GetWhy events anywhere.

• Grow the events function over time, including freelancers, agencies and future hires.

• Stay ahead of new event formats and technologies, and bring the best of them to GetWhy first.

Who you are

You’re not looking for an event coordination role. You’re a builder who sees events as the highest-leverage channel in a B2B enterprise sale, and you want to prove it on a global stage.

• 3–6+ years in event marketing, field marketing or experiential marketing for B2B SaaS, enterprise tech or a high-growth scale-up.

• A portfolio of standout events, with a track record that ties them directly to pipeline and revenue.

• Real taste. You know what makes a booth, a dinner or a keynote memorable, and you can explain why.

• Commercially minded. You think about pipeline and impact, not just logistics.

• A poster, not a scroller. Social media is second nature, and you know what makes an event clip worth watching.

• Comfortable behind a camera and in front of people. You can film, run an interview and do basic editing on the fly.

• A strong operator who can run several events in parallel across time zones without dropping quality.

• An excellent communicator who can brief a designer, negotiate with a venue and pitch an executive audience.

• Comfortable with CRM and marketing automation tools such as HubSpot or Salesforce.

• A willing traveler. You go where the events are and you bring the energy.

Bonus points

• Experience from the insights, market research or MarTech industry. You know the conferences, the audience and the culture.

• Experience at an AI-native research company or a frontier AI or tech company known for its events.

• You’ve built an events function from scratch, including playbooks, processes and measurement.

• You’ve produced a flagship owned event or customer conference.

• A network of event organisers, venues and production partners across Europe and the US.

What we offer

• A fast-scaling, ambitious company where events are a core growth engine, not an afterthought.

• The chance to build GetWhy’s global events function from the ground up and define how a category leader shows up in the world.

• Real ownership, a seat close to leadership, and the budget and trust to try bold ideas.

• Work with some of the world’s most influential brands as customers, speakers and partners.

• Annual company retreats and Friday bar events. We work hard, and we celebrate hard.

How to apply

Click apply and upload your CV, LinkedIn profile, and a link to a portfolio of events you’ve produced. Event photos, clips or social posts you’ve made are a big plus.

If we see a match, we’ll invite you to a conversation online or at our office. The process includes a short creative assignment, where you’ll pitch how GetWhy should show up at one of our key industry conferences.

This isn’t the easiest events job out there. It’s the one that will define how a category leader shows up in the world. Let’s build GetWhy together.

jobs.occupation: Service Manager Level 1 SCADA & Power Plant Control
jobs.description:
Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company driving the transition to a sustainable energy system. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years. We employ around 21 000 people mostly in our core markets in Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK.

Job Description

Are you an experienced SCADA engineer or technical service lead who wants to remain hands-on while taking responsibility for reliable service delivery? Would you like to combine solving technical problems with guiding colleagues and improving business-critical services supporting renewable energy?

As our new Service Manager Level 1 SCADA & Power Plant Control, you will be responsible for the reliable, secure and efficient delivery of agreed SCADA and Power Plant Control services supporting Vattenfall’s renewable-energy operations. Your scope includes WTG and substation SCADA, hybrid park controllers and interfaces to WTG Power Plant Controllers.

You will combine hands-on SCADA engineering and incident resolution with functional leadership of a dedicated service team of Level 1 SCADA and Power Plant Control engineers. Alongside your own technical assignments, you will prioritise the team’s work, coordinate suppliers and support functions, and drive continual improvement while meeting agreed service levels.

Working closely with customers, stakeholders and the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, you will help develop standardised, proactive service delivery that combines effective incident response with preventive maintenance, lifecycle planning and long-term service improvement.

Be in your element with BA Wind

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets.

You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

Qualifications

Y****our role

You will take responsibility for the delivery and performance of the services within your agreed scope, from their introduction into operation through ongoing support, improvement and eventual replacement or retirement.

Your service scope covers Level 1 SCADA for WTGs and substations, together with assigned Power Plant Control systems and interfaces, including hybrid park controllers and interfaces to WTG Power Plant Controllers. You will take responsibility for their operational support, controlled changes, lifecycle management and continual improvement within agreed ownership boundaries.

This role combines hands-on senior SCADA engineering with functional service leadership and does not include personnel line management. You will personally undertake engineering work while coordinating and prioritising the service team’s activities, monitoring outcomes and making risks, dependencies and resource needs visible. Capability and capacity requirements will be aligned with the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, with resources requested from the respective line managers.

You will apply your practical engineering expertise to diagnose faults, restore services and implement controlled technical changes within your agreed scope and authorisation. You will provide technical guidance to colleagues, assess operational risks and challenge proposed solutions, combining hands-on delivery with effective planning and coordination across organisational boundaries.

You will participate in the team’s on-call rotation, personally diagnosing and resolving incidents affecting SCADA and Power Plant Control services outside normal working hours, within your agreed technical scope and authorisation. You will involve other engineers, OEMs and suppliers when specialist support is required, follow agreed escalation arrangements and contribute to root-cause investigations and corrective and preventive actions.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Service scope and support arrangements: Maintaining clear service definitions, ownership boundaries, agreed service levels, support responsibilities and escalation arrangements, aligned with the agreed service mapping, the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager and customer expectations.

• Service delivery and hands-on engineering: Managing reliable, secure and efficient day-to-day delivery of SCADA and Power Plant Control services, including monitoring, incidents, service requests, problems, changes and lifecycle activities. Personally configuring, testing, commissioning, maintaining and improving assigned systems, controllers and interfaces within approved procedures and authorisations, while balancing engineering assignments with service-leadership responsibilities and agreed priorities.

• Service performance: Monitoring performance against agreed service-level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational targets. Reporting on service availability, incident response and restoration, recurring issues, risks and improvement actions.

• Incident response and problem management: Personally diagnosing and resolving incidents affecting assigned SCADA systems, Power Plant Control systems and interfaces, while coordinating additional engineers, OEMs, suppliers and support functions as required. Ensuring timely service restoration and clear stakeholder updates, investigating root causes and implementing or assigning corrective and preventive actions, with follow-up to completion.

• Backlog and delivery planning: Managing and prioritising the service team’s backlog, dependencies and delivery plans based on higher-level guidance, operational impact, risk and available capacity. Planning your own engineering assignments alongside service-leadership responsibilities, balancing urgent operational needs with planned maintenance, lifecycle work and improvements, and making capacity trade-offs visible.

• Capability and capacity planning: Identifying the skills and capacity required to deliver agreed services and roadmap commitments, aligning them with the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, and requesting resources from the respective line managers and making the consequences of resource gaps visible.

• Lifecycle engineering and controlled change: Executing the agreed service roadmap through hands-on engineering and coordination of upgrades, migrations, patching, configuration changes and lifecycle replacements. Preparing, implementing or reviewing assigned changes, with appropriate risk assessment, testing, rollback arrangements, documentation and operational handover through approved processes.

• Supplier and stakeholder coordination: Coordinating contributions from suppliers, specialists and internal support functions, monitoring delivery against agreed responsibilities and service commitments, and following up on issues. Supporting technical and service-related purchasing or contract discussions with the responsible procurement and contract owners.

• Project requirements and transition to operations: Providing OT operations and maintenance requirements to projects whose deliverables will enter the service team’s scope. Agreeing operational acceptance criteria with the relevant stakeholders and participating in readiness reviews and handovers, checking support coverage, monitoring, documentation, recovery arrangements and unresolved risks.

• Operational documentation and knowledge: Producing and maintaining technical records, configuration information, operational runbooks and troubleshooting guidance for your own engineering work. Ensuring that the service team maintains relevant service and asset records, clear support responsibilities, escalation arrangements and accessible operational knowledge.

• Continual improvement and technical guidance: Using service-performance data and operational experience to identify, prioritise and implement improvements that reduce recurring incidents and strengthen reliability, efficiency and supportability. Standardising repeatable services and work packages, contributing to technical reviews, and supporting colleagues through practical guidance, knowledge sharing and appropriate automation.

• Security, compliance and audit support: Ensuring that applicable cybersecurity, regulatory and operational requirements are incorporated into service delivery and lifecycle planning, in collaboration with the responsible service engineers, cybersecurity and compliance functions. Coordinating relevant evidence and follow-up actions for audits and reviews.

• Risk management and escalation: Maintaining visibility of service risks, dependencies, delivery constraints and outstanding decisions. Escalating issues beyond the service team’s mandate or capacity to the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager and other responsible stakeholders, with clear recommendations and operational consequences.

Your profile / who are you?

You hold a relevant bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, automation or control engineering, computer engineering, industrial IT, systems engineering or a related discipline. Alternatively, you have developed equivalent professional competence through a relevant technical qualification and substantial hands-on experience in SCADA or industrial OT engineering and operational support.

You have several years of hands-on experience engineering, operating and supporting SCADA systems or comparable industrial OT solutions, including recent practical experience diagnosing faults, restoring services and implementing controlled changes. You can personally diagnose faults, restore services and implement controlled technical changes. You have also demonstrated the ability to coordinate technical work, prioritise operational needs and guide colleagues or suppliers. Your background may be as a senior engineer, technical lead or service manager who has remained technically active; a previous formal Service Manager title is not required.

You understand the demands of supporting business-critical systems and can translate operational needs into clear priorities, responsibilities and delivery plans. You are comfortable taking responsibility for service outcomes while working with engineers, suppliers and line managers in a matrix organisation.

You have excellent written and spoken English skills and can communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. The role may be subject to security clearance, and candidates must be able to meet the applicable screening requirements.

You bring knowledge and experience in:

• Operational service management: Applying structured incident, problem, service-request, change, configuration and lifecycle-management practices, with clear ownership, service levels and follow-up.

• Hands-on SCADA engineering: Practical experience configuring, integrating, testing, commissioning, maintaining, operating and supporting SCADA systems and interfaces, including documenting and validating technical changes.

• SCADA and OT environments: Understanding the role of SCADA in asset monitoring and control, including interfaces and dependencies between WTG and substation systems, power plant control, central control systems and supporting infrastructure. You can engage meaningfully with specialists and assess the operational implications of technical proposals.

• Service leadership and prioritisation: Coordinating multidisciplinary service teams and suppliers, managing backlogs and dependencies, identifying capacity requirements and resolving competing priorities within an agreed mandate.

• Operational resilience and secure engineering: Practical experience supporting service availability through monitoring, backup and recovery of SCADA applications and configurations, secure access, vulnerability handling and controlled technical changes, in collaboration with the teams responsible for supporting infrastructure.

• Service introduction and handover: Translating operations and maintenance needs into project requirements and acceptance criteria, assessing operational readiness and coordinating the transition of new or changed solutions into supported services.

• Supplier and stakeholder management: Establishing clear expectations, following up on service commitments, coordinating across organisational boundaries and handling escalations constructively.

• Incident and problem management: Diagnosing faults across SCADA applications, Power Plant Control systems, interfaces and connected systems, including dependencies on server services, networks, certificates and service accounts. Personally restoring services within your technical scope and authorisation, investigating root causes and implementing corrective and preventive actions, with specialist or supplier support where required.

• Performance analysis and improvement: Using service metrics, incident trends, risks and operational feedback to identify improvement priorities, track actions and communicate progress and results.

Additional experience that would be valuable:

• Experience with wind-turbine and substation SCADA platforms, hybrid park controllers, or OEM-specific WTG Power Plant Controllers and their interfaces.

• ITIL or comparable service-management training, or relevant OT cybersecurity training.

• Experience with service-management, backlog-planning, reporting and knowledge-management tools.

Personal traits

To succeed in this role, we believe that you:

• Take ownership of service outcomes and follow through on commitments, decisions and improvement actions.

• Lead through clear priorities, constructive challenge and collaboration, including where you do not have direct line authority.

• Remain calm and decisive during operational incidents, communicating clearly and involving the right people at the right time.

• Work in a structured and transparent way, making risks, dependencies, resource constraints and delivery progress visible.

• Use sound judgement to balance immediate service restoration, operational risk, long-term reliability, maintainability and agreed delivery priorities.

• Build effective relationships across engineering, Operations, projects, suppliers and support functions, and actively encourage knowledge sharing.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Location: Kolding, Denmark or Amsterdam, Netherlands

Additional Information

Our offer

Looking for a career with growth?

Looking for a role where your superpowers can be leveraged to the maximum and with limitless opportunities for growth?

The scale and ambition of our wind, battery and solar business means you can

At Intempus, our goal is simple: make time tracking as easy, intelligent and automated as it can possibly be. We're building the future of time tracking and our ambitions are high. This means that our system needs to deliver a stable and great user experience at all times — especially since our user base keeps growing fast.

That’s why we're looking for you: an experienced DevOps Engineer ready for the challenge.

What we offer

• 
A role where you can grow, learn and make a real impact

• 
A helpful, social and diverse workplace with a flat hierarchy and open communication

• 
A healthy work/life balance

• 
55 friendly, driven and skilled colleagues

• 
Flexibility, including two days of remote work per week

• 
A centrally located, modern office at Visma House in Carlsberg Byen, Copenhagen

• 
… and much more!

Your role

As part of our four people DevOps team, your main responsibility will be keeping our systems running smoothly around the clock. More specifically, you will:

• 
Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines that ensure fast, reliable and secure delivery of changes to our applications

• 
Automate infrastructure and server configuration using tools like Ansible, Terraform or whatever fits best — we're moving from a fully manual setup to infrastructure and configuration that's fully documented and managed as code

• 
Monitor and troubleshoot day-to-day issues across our servers and applications

• 
Design and implement improvements using the best tools the DevOps ecosystem has to offer — anything from a new secrets management solution to better container deployment workflows

• 
Collaborate with developers to improve tooling around development and test environments

• 
Keep our infrastructure and applications updated and secure

• 
Automate wherever possible, to cut down on manual effort and maintenance overhead

Who are you?

You're proactive and take ownership of your work. You thrive in a team with plenty of freedom, where ideas are shared openly and people genuinely listen to and support each other.

You communicate clearly, both in writing and in person, and you actively help foster a good team environment.

You hold a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent, and you bring at least 7 years of experience in a DevOps role or similar (e.g. System Administrator).

On the technical side, you have experience with:

• 
Managing Linux systems for at least two years (we run Debian-based Linux across all our servers)

• 
Bash scripting — you're comfortable working in a bash shell

• 
Docker — building, testing, deploying and maintaining containerized applications in production

• 
A programming language (our CI/CD pipeline and much of our automation is written in Python)

• 
git

• 
A CI/CD tool (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.)

• 
An infrastructure-as-code tool, ideally Terraform

• 
A configuration management tool, ideally Ansible

• 
Container orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes, HashiCorp Nomad)

Nice to have, but not required:

• 
Managing PostgreSQL databases

• 
Cloud services with any provider

Who are we?

Intempus is a Danish software company with offices in Copenhagen and Aarhus. Since 2012, we've built, refined and optimized our own time-tracking system, and we continue to hold high ambitions for our product.

Our team of 55 includes a development team of 35 driven engineers. We are part of the Visma Group but operate day-to-day as an independent company.

Take a look at our team in the Copenhagen office here!

Ready to join us?

Apply now if you can see yourself as our new DevOps Engineer. Job start is January 1st, 2027, but we are flexible for the right candidate. The role is on-site at our office at Visma House in Carlsberg Byen, Copenhagen.

Please submit your application in English, as we are an international team, and include your resumé, educational diploma and references.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Responsibilities and technologies

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Developing and maintaining risk scenarios, assessing the effectiveness of mitigating controls against the scenarios, and conducting risk assessments to support business decisions

• Establishing automated measurements and KPIs that provide insight into the implementation and effectiveness of security controls across the business

• Interpreting regulatory and contractual security requirements and translating these into Netcompany's security baselines and standard methodologies

• Planning and executing security awareness activities, including phishing simulations, targeted micro-learning, and onboarding/yearly awareness training

To succeed in this role you:

The Mission: Build the Next Generation of SBC Systems

Ibsen Photonics develops Spectral Beam Combining (SBC) modules for high-power laser architectures, based on our in-house transmission gratings. We are looking for a Laser Engineer to join the High-Power Beam Combining team and contribute across design, assembly, and experimental optimisation of these modules, working closely with colleagues and international partners.

What you will do

• Design and assemble compact SBC modules based on Ibsen's transmission gratings, accounting for optical beam paths, thermal effects, and mechanical constraints

• Optimise optical alignment, mechanical stability, and thermal management at high power loads in iterative design–experiment–optimise cycles

• Characterise beam quality during power scaling, including M², wavefront sensing, and spectral analysis

• Support sourcing of optical and mechanical components and the transition from experimental prototypes to scalable, volume-ready designs

• Collaborate with internal teams and international partners, including occasional overseas visits for joint prototyping and testing

What you bring

You are a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a "build-test-learn" environment.

Ideally, you possess

• MSc or PhD in optics, photonics, laser physics, or a related field

• Documented laboratory experience with high-power optics and/or lasers

• Knowledge of high-power-capable optical design practices, including thermal lensing, runaway effects, and their mitigation, as well as Gaussian optics and beam propagation

• Knowledge of opto-mechanical design practices for high-power devices

• Hands-on experience with precise free-space and/or fibre optical alignment and experimental troubleshooting

• Experience with beam quality measurement and analysis

• Professional proficiency in English

Nice to have

• Experience with SBC or CBC techniques

• Mechanical design of tight-tolerance devices and familiarity with mechanical CAD

• Experience transitioning prototypes toward volume production

• Proficiency in optical simulation tools (e.g. Zemax)
